# Changelog

Version history, new features, and breaking changes for Pushary

Updated

## Phone calls, November 18, 2026

Versions covered by this entry:

- CLI (`pushary`, also published as `@pushary/agent-hooks`): 1.9.142 to 1.9.184
- Pushary app for iPhone and Android: 1.0.61

Pushary can call your phone when an agent waits on a request you did not answer. The push still comes first. If the request is still waiting after Call after, Pushary calls you, reads the request and takes your answer. Calls shipped as a beta on November 12 and left beta on November 15. The Phone calls guide covers setup, the agents that can be called, the countries Pushary can call and every limit.

### Security [...] - The Calls page. Since November 17, Calls is its own page in the dashboard sidebar. It holds your number, the test call, your rules, your minutes and Call history, with a transcript of each call kept for 30 days. Links to the old Phone calls tab in Settings open it.
- `pushary calls`. With CLI 1.9.161, `npx pushary@latest calls on` asks for your number and first name, places the test call, waits for you to confirm the number, asks you to agree to the calls and turns them on. `pushary calls` shows whether they are on, and `pushary calls off` stops them. CLI reference [...] - A notice when a key changes your number. When an API key sets a new number or turns calls on, Pushary sends a push to your paired phone and an email, both showing the number in full. Keys can make five such changes for you in 24 hours, counted across all your keys. After that, a key's change is refused, and you set your number or turn calls on in the dashboard. Since CLI 1.9.184, `pushary calls on` says so when it is refused for that reason.
- "Call me if you get stuck." Since CLI 1.9.144, the instructions and the skill Pushary installs tell an agent what to do when you ask it to call you: ask through `ask_user`. The reply says whether a call is planned, and the agent is told not to promise one when none is.
